items.d: 삼성전자가 하만(HARMAN)의 대표 오디오 브랜드 JBL의 80주년과 바워스앤윌킨스(Bowers & Wilkins) 60주년을 기념하는 특별 행사를 개최한다. 삼성전자는 24일부터 31일까지 서울 강남구 ‘프로젝트 스페이스 라인(Project Space Line)’에서 ‘사운드 레전드 – JBL 80주년 기념 전시 및 바워스앤윌킨스 60주년 기념 전시(Sound Legends – Celebrating 80 Years of JBL and 60 Years of Bowers & Wilkins)’를 연다. 올해는 JBL이 80주년, […]
items.fullText: 삼성전자, JBL 80주년·바워스앤윌킨스 60주년 특별 기념 행사 개최 2026/10/21 AUDIO Play Download 공유 레이어 열기 인쇄하기 삼성전자가 하만(HARMAN)의 대표 오디오 브랜드 JBL의 80주년과 바워스앤윌킨스(Bowers & Wilkins) 60주년을 기념하는 특별 행사를 개최한다. 삼성전자는 24일부터 31일까지 서울 강남구 ‘프로젝트 스페이스 라인(Project Space Line)’에서 ‘사운드 레전드 – JBL 80주년 기념 전시 및 바워스앤윌킨스 60주년 기념 전시(Sound Legends – Celebrating 80 Years of JBL and 60 Years of Bowers & Wilkins)’를 연다. 올해는 JBL이 80주년, 바워스앤윌킨스 60주년을 맞는 해이자 삼성전자가 하만 인수를 발표한 지 10년이 되는 해다. 삼성전자는 이번 행사를 통해 두 브랜드의 시대별 대표 제품과 최신 모델을 함께 선보이며, 전문 음향 기술이 일상으로 확장된 과정과 원음 재현을 위한 기술 발전의 역사를 소개한다. 하만은 JBL 80주년을 기념해 올해 암스테르담, 로스앤젤레스, 뮌헨, 뉴욕, 도쿄, 빈 등 세계 주요 도시를 순회하며 80년간의 대표 제품과 혁신의 여정을 소개하는 ‘JBL 플레이백 갤러리(JBL Playback Gallery)’ 행사를 진행하고 있다. 이번 서울 행사도 글로벌 순회 행사의 일환으로 마련됐다. ▲ JBL 모델이 21일 서울 삼성동 프로젝트 스페이스 라인에 위치한 JBL 80주년 및 바워스 앤 월킨스 60주년 특별 전시관에서 JBL 80주년 기념 로고를 소개하고 있다. 80년간 음악이 필요한 모든 순간에 함께한 JBL 사운드 혁신 선보여 JBL은 1946년 미국의 음향 엔지니어 제임스 B. 랜싱(James B. Lansing)이 설립한 오디오 브랜드다. 음악이 필요한 모든 순간을 함께하겠다는 브랜드 철학을 바탕으로 록 페스티벌의 시초로 불리는 우드스탁(Woodstock) 페스티벌부터 영화관과 레코딩 스튜디오, 가정용 오디오, 스마트 기기에 이르기까지 다양한 환경에 맞춘 음향 기술을 선보였으며, 80년간 이어진 사운드 혁신을 통해 음악을 경험하는 방식을 변화시켜 왔다. 하만은 1969년 JBL을 인수하며 글로벌 초일류 오디오 기업으로 본격적으로 성장하기 시작했으며 현재 JBL을 중심으로 글로벌 포터블 오디오 시장에서 1위를 지키고 있다. 행사는 JBL의 역사를 소개하는 영상 상영과 사진 전시, 대표 레거시 제품과 인기 모델의 전시·시연으로 구성됐다. 행사장 1층에서는 JBL이 써내려간 사운드의 80년 역사의 발자취를 보여주는 영상과 사진을 만나볼 수 있다. 2층에서는 ▲JBL 사운드의 뿌리를 보여주는 1920년대 ‘잭슨-벨 라디오(Jackson-Bell Radio)’ ▲1957년 출시된 ‘파라곤(Paragon)’ ▲1970년 출시된 ‘L100 센츄리(L100 Century)’ 스피커 등 시대별 대표 제품을 직접 보고 들을 수 있다. 잭슨-벨 라디오는 JBL 창립자 제임스 B. 랜싱이 초기 음향 기술 개발에 참여했던 시기를 보여주는 진공관 라디오로, JBL이 추구하는 강력하고 생생한 사운드 철학의 출발점을 보여주는 제품이다. JBL의 대표적인 헤리티지 제품인 파라곤(Paragon)은 좌우 스피커와 독창적인 음향 반사 구조를 하나의 대형 캐비닛에 담은 상징적인 스테레오 스피커다. 1957년 출시 이후 뛰어난 음향 성능과 혁신적인 디자인으로 JBL을 대표하는 오디오 명기로 평가받고 있다. 산업 디자이너 아놀드 울프(Arnold Wolf)가 디자인했으며, 스피커 본연의 기능에 조형미를 더해 공간을 완성하는 오브제로서의 역할도 한다. items.t: Stord Acquires AMS Fulfillment in Nine-Figure Deal
items.d:
E-Commerce logistics provider Stord made its largest acquisition to date acquiring competitor AMS Fulfillment. The deal includes 10 warehouses, which will bring Stord's global network to over 100 locations. 
Sean Henry, CEO and founder of Stord discusses the deal as well as the overall outlook for the shipping and logistics space. (Source: Bloomberg)

SpaceX and Tesla boards form special committees to review merger
items.d: Elon Musk likes the idea but says he is not on either committee, which is made up of independent directors.
items.fullText: The boards of SpaceX and Tesla have each formed special committees to review a possible merger. The special committees, which consist of independent directors, were created at the request of shareholders, according to Elon Musk, CEO and the largest individual shareholder of both companies. “Because I’m a conflicted party, I can’t actually be in the discussions of the special committees, so it’s this sort of a … It’s an odd kabuki dance where two groups of people are talking, and I can’t be in the conversation,” Musk said in response to a question during SpaceX’s third-quarter earnings call. Musk didn’t name the members of these special committees, only noting that they were independent directors. Tesla has seven independent board members under Nasdaq’s listing standards, including board chair Robyn Denholm; Ira Ehrenpreis, who is also a committee chair; former Tesla CTO JB Straubel; Joe Gebbia; Jack Hartung; James Murdoch; and Kathleen Wilson-Thompson, according to the company’s October 19 proxy filing . Neither Musk nor his brother Kimbal Musk is independent. Denholm, Gebbia, Ehrenpreis, Hartung, Murdoch, and Wilson-Thompson sit on a variety of established committees overseeing audit, compensation, and corporate governance. SpaceX lists six independent directors , including Ehrenpreis, who is also the chair of the company’s compensation and nominating committee. Randy Glein, Donald Harrison, Steve Jurvetson, Luke Nosek, and Roelof Botha are also considered independent directors. Antonio Gracias, Musk, and SpaceX president and chief operating officer Gwynne Shotwell are also on the board, but not considered independent. Gracias, who once sat on Tesla’s board, founded and leads Valor Equity Partners, which has a 3.4% stake in SpaceX. items.t: Elon Musk says SpaceX and Tesla have formed special committees to discuss merger idea
items.d: Musk said he isn’t a member of either special committee or involved in the talks because he’s a conflicted party under securities regulations.
items.fullText: Business News Elon Musk says SpaceX and Tesla have formed special committees to discuss merger idea Musk said he isn’t a member of either special committee or involved in the talks because he’s a conflicted party under securities regulations. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk said he favored combining his two biggest companies. Finn Gomez / Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Oct. 20, 2026, 6:57 PM EDT By David Ingram Tech billionaire Elon Musk said Tuesday that the boards of SpaceX and Tesla had separately formed special committees to discuss the idea of a merger, taking a small step toward the possible consolidation of his two biggest companies. Musk, who is the CEO of both companies, said that the special committees had not reached an agreement and that there was no guarantee they would. He said a merger would require support from both sets of shareholders. “I think some people out there assume that a SpaceX and Tesla merger is a certainty, and I think that would be overstating it,” he said. Musk spoke about the potential tie-up during a call with Wall Street analysts about SpaceX’s quarterly results, which surpassed estimates; the company’s revenue more than doubled in part from renting out computing capacity to other artificial intelligence firms. There has been intense speculation in the stock market over whether a combination might happen, and the two companies already overlap in some areas, including semiconductor manufacturing . In January, Tesla announced that it was investing about $2 billion to acquire shares in an AI startup that’s a subsidiary of SpaceX. Musk said that, because he’s a conflicted party under securities regulations, he is not a member of either special committee or involved in the talks. He said the committees consist of the two boards’ independent directors but did not specify the memberships. items.t: SpaceX’s AI business is beating expectations
items.d: SpaceX hit profitability in the third quarter, with net income of $4.4 billion. AI was the engine.
items.fullText: SpaceX’s data centers and Grok agents were more profitable than investors expected in the third quarter of the year, as the company leaves its roots as a space company behind to focus on artificial intelligence, which now makes up 52% of its income. CEO Elon Musk’s deep tech conglomerate reported $14.6 billion in third-quarter revenue on Tuesday, according to its regulatory filing . That number was driven by growth in all segments, but especially its renamed “Super Intelligence” business line, which generated $7.5 billion in revenue from the recently acquired Cursor coding tool, Grok bot, and most importantly, the company’s burgeoning neocloud business, which now boasts 1.7 GW of compute. The AI business generated $431 million in profit, which would have been higher without $1.2 billion in one-time stock-based compensation expenses related to the Cursor acquisition. The top-line revenue number was also boosted by about $1 billion in income related to the recovery of Bitcoin prices and unspecified related-party income that might be attributed to a SpaceX investment in another company. The growing revenue is balanced against total capital expenditures of $19.6 billion, as SpaceX continues to build out a second data center project, Colossus II, and increase investment in Starship, the heavy-lift rocket it sees as vital to deploying a new generation of Starlink satellites and developing orbital data centers. CFO Bret Johnsen said the company would spend $35 billion to $40 billion on new capital investments in the fourth quarter.
